output.question: Has LinkedIn announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. Reuters reported on May 13, 2026 that LinkedIn planned to inform staff of layoffs and intended to cut about 5% of its headcount as it reorganized teams and focused on growth areas. Reuters also reported that the rationale was not to replace LinkedIn jobs with artificial intelligence; as of November 11, 2026, the latest official LinkedIn company-post feed I retrieved (through November 9) did not contain a newer direct layoff announcement.

key_facts.fact: LinkedIn planned to inform staff of layoffs on May 13, 2026.
The planned reduction was about 5% of LinkedIn's headcount.
The reported rationale was reorganizing teams and focusing personnel on areas where the business was growing, rather than AI replacing jobs at LinkedIn.
The retrieved official LinkedIn company-post feed included posts through November 9, 2026, but no direct layoff announcement appeared in the retrieved results.

passages.quote: LinkedIn planned to inform staff of layoffs on Wednesday, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a widening of technology sector cuts this year.

The Microsoft-owned social network plans to cut about 5% of its headcount as it reorganizes teams and focuses personnel on areas where its business is growing, said one of the people, on condition of anonymity.
The layoff rationale was not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn, one of the people told Reuters.

caveats: Reuters attributed the May 2026 details to two people familiar with the matter, including one source speaking anonymously; LinkedIn's official company-post feed retrieved in this run did not itself contain the layoff announcement.
The 5% figure was reported as a planned cut, and Reuters said it was unable to determine which teams were affected.
The absence of a newer layoff post in the retrieved LinkedIn feed does not prove that no later internal or regional layoffs occurred.
